speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; to determine the cause, are you experiencing significant pain, redness, or warmth in the joint? Has this swelling been present continuously or does it come and go, and does it improve with rest or activity?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (Oligoarticular type) or early onset Blau syndrome (given family history of uncle with similar issues).
